messages:
alice-h: quick note - canary showed a spike in slow-path fallbacks for qwen-14b yesterday overnight. fallback rate ~20% on A100 cluster, started ~03:12 UTC.
ben-ops: saw it too. traces point to kernel selector rejecting flash paths and using SDPA/Triton slow path. repro on a100 around 03:14.
perf-bot: ALERT: fallback_rate_5m=19.6% service=inference-hosted env=canary (2026-03-17T03:12:00Z)
carmen-m: repro I used (local):
```
REDWOOD_MODELS=qwen-14b BATCH=8 SEQ=512 ./tools/infer_bench --profile --gpu a100
```
output: flash_kernel: REJECT head_dim=12 (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_SHAPE) -> fallback sdpa_tuned
jordan-r: head_dim=12 (not 8/16 aligned) 12-bit head widths frequently miss optimized flash kernels. usually batcher avoids mixing those, so fallback should be rare.
mei-ml: microbench results (H100 vs A100):
- flash (aligned 16) @ H100: 3800 tok/s
- sdpa fallback @ A100 (head_dim=12): 1100 tok/s
p95 latency: 38ms -> 142ms for seq=512, bs=8 when fallback path used.
tomas-k: two possible root causes:
1) batcher merge heuristic is combining requests across models with different head dims -> increases rejection surface.
2) kvcache mask offset + RoPE-scale logic when prefix caching is used can make selector compute conservative mask compatibility (false negative), forcing safe fallback.
alice-h: @tomas-k can you point to the kvcache module? I noticed offsets.py casts modulo values to signed ints in one branch which could produce negative remainder for certain large prefix offsets.
ben-ops: runtime log snippet from canary: 
```
[selector] model=qwen-14b head_dim=12 seq=512 -> candidate=flashattn_v2 rejected(reason=unaligned_head_width)
[selector] model=mistral-7b head_dim=64 -> candidate=flashattn_v2 accepted
[batcher] merging streams: models=[qwen-14b,mistral-7b] -> merged_heads=[12,64] -> merged=true
```
carmen-m: minimal repro to trigger mask issue with prefix caching:
```
# create prefix, then continue streaming
prefix_len=1200
generate(prefix)
next_request -> kernel error: mask_index OOB -> fallback to sdpa
```
jordan-r: hypothesis: RoPE scale multiplier shifts computed pos indices so that mask index checks used by selector see an out-of-range position for certain prefix+seq combos, selector then declines flash path.
mei-ml: quick experiment: disabled cross-model merging when head dims differ (strict split). fallback_rate dropped from ~20% -> ~4% on mixed workload, overall throughput up ~25%.
perf-bot: experiment logged: exp_id=exp-20260317-batch-split-v2 metrics=[fallback_rate,p95_latency,tokens_per_sec]
tomas-k: suggested config (draft):
```
batching:
  allow_cross_model_merge: conditional
  merge_rules:
    - key: head_dim_align
      require_mod: 8
    - key: rope_scale
      require_equal: true
```
alice-h: also propose a seq_len gate: only enforce strict head alignment check when seq_len >= 256. small queries benefit from flash even if head_dim%8!=0 and risk is low.
ben-ops: agree. rollout plan: patch -> canary 10% traffic tomorrow; monitor fallback_rate & p95. rollback if fallback_rate > 10% or p95 > 2x baseline. I'll create dashboard and alerts.
carmen-m: I'll open PR to add kvcache offset unit tests and an integration test that reproduces the mask OOB with prefixes. will include a short-form reproducer script.
jordan-r: I'll update kernel selector to add a platform relax flag (enable_unaligned_flash_on_h100) and expose it behind a feature flag for gradual enable.
mei-ml: recommend adding model metadata flag in catalog: `supports_unaligned_flash=true|false` so operators can opt models in/out and batcher can use that metadata.
alice-h: owners & next steps: carmen-m (kvcache tests + repro), jordan-r (selector PR + feature flag), tomas-k (batcher config change + canary plan), ben-ops (dashboards/rollout). target: canary tomorrow 10% then ramp if metrics good. :rocket:
perf-bot: TODO assigned -> carmen-m (kvcache repro), jordan-r (selector PR), tomas-k (batcher config).
alice-h: thanks everyone. if anyone nails a smaller reproducible case that triggers only the mask OOB please paste it here. :bug:
